title: The Book of Zechariah Timeline
sub: Eight Night Visions · Your King Comes Riding on a Donkey
desc: A sequence of symbolic night visions gives way to some of the most directly Messianic material in the Old Testament — a king entering on a donkey, thirty pieces of silver thrown to a potter, and one they have pierced whom Jerusalem will mourn.

eras.label: Era One · Zechariah 1
eras.name: Turn to Me — the Man Among the Myrtle Trees
eras.dates: A call to repentance opens a book that will spend most of its length in symbolic night visions, beginning with a rider surveying a strangely peaceful world

events.title: Turn to Me, and I Will Turn to You
events.detail: Zechariah opens with a direct appeal not to repeat the ancestors' stubbornness, noting that though the earlier prophets are long dead, their words outlived them and proved true.

verses.text: “‘Turn to me,’ says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies, ‘and I will turn to you,’ says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies.”

events.title: The Man Among the Myrtle Trees — How Long Before You Have Compassion?
events.detail: The first of eight night visions shows riders patrolling the earth and reporting it strangely at rest, prompting the angel of the LORD to ask how long Jerusalem's 70-year desolation will continue, answered with a promise to rebuild the temple.

verses.text: “‘I have become compassionate toward Jerusalem and will rebuild my temple in it,’ says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies.”

eras.label: Era Two · Zechariah 2
eras.name: Four Horns and Four Blacksmiths — a Wall of Fire Around Jerusalem
eras.dates: Two more night visions promise both the destruction of the powers that scattered Israel and an unwalled, divinely-protected future for Jerusalem. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls earlier than most English translations, marked inline in the NET text as “(2:1)” and “(2:5)”; references here may run a few verses higher than in an English Bible for this chapter.)

events.title: Four Horns and Four Blacksmiths
events.detail: Four horns representing the powers that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem are met by four blacksmiths sent specifically to terrify and cut those horns down. (Numbered 1:18-21 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “The blacksmiths have come to terrify Judah's enemies and cut off the horns of the nations that have thrust themselves against the land of Judah.” (Numbered 1:21 in most English translations.)

events.title: I Will Be a Wall of Fire Surrounding Jerusalem
events.detail: A man with a measuring line intends to survey Jerusalem's dimensions, but is told the city will grow too large for walls at all — the LORD himself will be a wall of fire around it and the source of glory within it. (Numbered 2:1-13 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “‘I,’ the LORD [Yahweh] says, ‘will be a wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem and the source of glory in her midst.’” (Numbered 2:5 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Three · Zechariah 3
eras.name: Joshua the High Priest — My Servant the Branch
eras.dates: A courtroom vision clears the high priest of accusation and introduces a title — the Branch — that will recur throughout the rest of the book

events.title: Satan Accuses Joshua — I Am About to Introduce My Servant, the Branch
events.detail: The high priest Joshua stands accused by Satan while wearing filthy garments, but the angel of the LORD rebukes the accuser and reclothes him in clean garments, declaring him a symbol pointing toward a coming servant called the Branch.

verses.text: “I am about to introduce my servant, the Branch… I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day.”

eras.label: Era Four · Zechariah 4
eras.name: Not by Strength, Not by Power, But by My Spirit
eras.dates: A golden lampstand flanked by two olive trees delivers one of the most quoted single verses in the whole book, aimed directly at Zerubbabel's rebuilding project

events.title: Not by Strength, Not by Power, but by My Spirit
events.detail: A golden lampstand fed by two olive trees becomes a vision assuring Zerubbabel that the temple's completion depends not on human strength but on the LORD's own Spirit, with the mountain of opposition destined to become a level plain before him.

verses.text: “This is the LORD's [Yahweh's] message to Zerubbabel: ‘Not by strength and not by power, but by my Spirit,’ says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies.”

eras.label: Era Five · Zechariah 5
eras.name: The Flying Scroll and the Woman in the Basket
eras.dates: Two more visions personify sin itself as both a curse that enters households and a wickedness carried away to a temple of its own

events.title: A Flying Scroll of Curses — Wickedness Carried Away in a Basket
events.detail: A massive flying scroll represents a curse entering the houses of thieves and false swearers, followed by a vision of wickedness personified as a woman sealed inside a basket and carried off to Babylon — sin removed from the land entirely.

verses.text: “This is a curse traveling across the whole earth. For example, whoever steals will be removed from the community.”

eras.label: Era Six · Zechariah 6
eras.name: Four Chariots — Behold the Man Whose Name Is Branch
eras.dates: The final night vision sends chariots to patrol the earth's four directions, followed by an enacted coronation prophecy naming the coming Branch

events.title: Four Chariots — the Four Spirits of Heaven
events.detail: The eighth and final night vision sends four chariots out to patrol the four directions of the earth on the LORD's behalf, closing the sequence of symbolic visions that opened the book.

verses.text: “These are the four spirits of heaven going out after presenting themselves before the LORD [Yahweh] of all the earth.”

events.title: Behold the Man Whose Name Is Branch — a Priest on the Throne
events.detail: In an enacted prophecy, a crown is placed on the high priest Joshua's head as a sign of a coming figure called the Branch, who will build the temple, sit as both king and priest on his throne, with peaceful counsel between the two offices.

verses.text: “Here is the man whose name is Branch, who will sprout up from his place and build the temple of the LORD [Yahweh]… he will be a priest on his throne.”

eras.label: Era Seven · Zechariah 7
eras.name: A Question About Fasting — True Judgment, Mercy, and Compassion
eras.dates: A delegation asking about ritual fasting receives an answer that redirects attention entirely toward ethical obedience

events.title: Should We Weep in the Fifth Month, As We Have Done for Years?
events.detail: A delegation from Bethel asks whether they should continue a fast commemorating the temple's destruction, and the LORD responds by questioning whether their fasting, or even their feasting, was ever really for him at all.

verses.text: “When you fasted and lamented in the fifth and seventh months through all these 70 years, did you truly fast for me—for me, indeed?”

events.title: Exercise True Judgment — They Made Their Hearts as Hard as Diamond
events.detail: The real requirement is named directly — true justice, brotherhood, and compassion for the widow, orphan, foreigner, and poor — and the ancestors' stubborn refusal to listen is why the land was eventually swept into exile among nations they didn't know.

verses.text: “Exercise true judgment and show brotherhood and compassion to each other. You must not oppress the widow, the orphan, the resident foreigner, or the poor.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Zechariah 8
eras.name: Old Men and Boys Playing in the Streets — God Is With You
eras.dates: A cascade of ten short promises paints a picture of restored, peaceful, prosperous Jerusalem, closing in a vision of nations desperate to attach themselves to God's people

events.title: I Have Returned to Zion — Old Men and Boys Playing in the Streets
events.detail: A series of promises describes a restored Jerusalem full of the ordinary signs of peace — elderly residents sitting in the plazas, children playing in the streets — replacing the curse of the nations with a call to become a blessing instead.

verses.text: “‘I have returned to Zion and will live within Jerusalem,’” says the LORD [Yahweh]. “‘Now Jerusalem will be called “truthful city.”’”

events.title: Ten People From Every Nation Will Grasp the Robe of One Jew
events.detail: Fasts turn into joyful feasts, and the chapter closes with a striking image of the nations so eager to find God that ten people from every language will grab hold of a single Jewish person's robe just to go with them.

verses.text: “‘Ten people from all languages and nations will grasp hold of—indeed, grab—the robe of one Jew and say, “Let us go with you, for we have heard that God [Elohim] is with you.”’”

eras.label: Era Nine · Zechariah 9
eras.name: Judgment on the Nations — Your King Is Coming, Riding on a Donkey
eras.dates: A new section of oracles opens with judgment on Israel's neighbors before delivering the book's most famous single prophecy, quoted directly at Jesus's entry into Jerusalem

events.title: Judgment on Damascus, Tyre, and the Philistine Cities
events.detail: Judgment falls on the wealthy trading city of Tyre and the Philistine cities, though even Philistia's survivors are promised eventual inclusion among the people of God, while the LORD promises to personally guard his temple from invaders.

verses.text: “I will surround my temple to protect it like a guard from anyone crossing back and forth… for now I myself have seen it.”

events.title: Your King Is Coming to You, Riding on a Donkey
events.detail: Zion is told to rejoice because its king is coming, humble and victorious, riding not a warhorse but a donkey — a prophecy fulfilled exactly on the first Palm Sunday and quoted directly in the Gospels.

verses.text: “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Look! Your king is coming to you… riding on a donkey.”

eras.label: Era Ten · Zechariah 10
eras.name: Ask the LORD for Rain — I Will Strengthen Them
eras.dates: False shepherds relying on idols and omens are contrasted with the LORD's promise to personally regather and strengthen his scattered flock

events.title: The Shepherds Have Led Them Astray — I Will Strengthen the House of Judah
events.detail: False shepherds relying on household idols and lying omens have scattered the flock like sheep without a shepherd, but the LORD promises to personally gather, redeem, and strengthen his people from every land they've been scattered into.

verses.text: “I will restore them; I have compassion on them, and they will be as though I had never rejected them, for I am the LORD [Yahweh] their God [Elohim].”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Zechariah 11
eras.name: The Foolish and Worthless Shepherds — Thirty Pieces of Silver
eras.dates: A prophet enacts the role of a rejected shepherd, receiving an insultingly low wage that is thrown to a potter — a scene Matthew directly connects to Judas's betrayal

events.title: Thirty Pieces of Silver — Thrown to the Potter in the LORD's House
events.detail: Zechariah acts out the role of a shepherd, breaking two staffs named Pleasantness and Union to symbolize a broken covenant and fractured brotherhood, paid an insultingly low thirty pieces of silver which he throws to the potter in the LORD's own house — a scene Matthew's Gospel directly ties to Judas's betrayal price.

verses.text: “They weighed out my wages—thirty pieces of silver… ‘Throw it to the potter,’ the LORD [Yahweh] said to me… I threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD [Yahweh].”

events.title: The Equipment of a Foolish Shepherd
events.detail: In contrast to the good shepherd just enacted, Zechariah is told to take up the role of a worthless shepherd who abandons the flock entirely — a woe pronounced against exactly the kind of leadership Israel would soon experience.

verses.text: “Woe to the worthless shepherd who abandons the flock! May a sword fall on his arm and his right eye!”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Zechariah 12
eras.name: Jerusalem a Heavy Stone — They Will Look on Me, the One They Have Pierced
eras.dates: A siege of Jerusalem becomes the occasion for one of the most striking Messianic prophecies in the Old Testament, later applied directly to the crucifixion in John's Gospel

events.title: Jerusalem a Cup That Brings Dizziness — a Heavy Stone for All Nations
events.detail: All the surrounding nations gather against Jerusalem, but the LORD promises to make the city an immovable, injuring burden for anyone who tries to lift it, defending even its weakest inhabitants like mighty David.

verses.text: “I will make Jerusalem a heavy burden for all the nations, and all who try to carry it will be seriously injured.”

events.title: They Will Look on Me, the One They Have Pierced
events.detail: A spirit of grace and supplication poured out on Jerusalem produces mourning for someone the LORD identifies as pierced by his own people — a prophecy the Gospel of John quotes directly, applying it to the crucifixion.

verses.text: “They will look to me, the one they have pierced. They will lament for him as one laments for an only son.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Zechariah 13
eras.name: A Fountain Opened for Sin — Strike the Shepherd
eras.dates: A cleansing fountain and a purge of false prophecy lead into a strike-the-shepherd prophecy Jesus applies directly to himself and his disciples at the Last Supper

events.title: A Fountain Opened to Cleanse Sin — False Prophets Removed
events.detail: A cleansing fountain is opened for David's dynasty and Jerusalem's people, accompanied by the complete removal of false prophecy from the land, so thorough that future prophets will hide their identity out of shame.

verses.text: “In that day there will be a fountain opened up for the dynasty of David and the people of Jerusalem to cleanse them from sin and impurity.”

events.title: Strike the Shepherd, and the Sheep Will Be Scattered
events.detail: A sword is commanded against the LORD's own shepherd, scattering the flock, before a refining process purges two-thirds of the people and leaves a tested remnant who genuinely call on the LORD's name — a verse Jesus quotes directly of himself and his disciples in Matthew 26.

verses.text: “Awake, sword, against my shepherd, against the man who is my associate,” says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies. “Strike the shepherd that the flock may be scattered.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Zechariah 14
eras.name: The LORD's Feet on the Mount of Olives — the LORD Will Be King Over All the Earth
eras.dates: The book's climactic final chapter describes the LORD himself physically intervening at Jerusalem, splitting the Mount of Olives, and being crowned king over the whole earth

events.title: His Feet Will Stand on the Mount of Olives — the Mountain Split in Two
events.detail: After the nations besiege Jerusalem, the LORD himself goes out to fight, his feet landing on the Mount of Olives and splitting it in two to create an escape valley, producing living waters that flow out toward both the eastern and western seas.

verses.text: “His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives that lies to the east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in half from east to west.”

events.title: The LORD Will Be King Over All the Earth
events.detail: The book closes with a vision of universal worship — the LORD reigning as one king with one name over the whole earth, surviving nations required to celebrate the Feast of Shelters annually, and even ordinary cooking pots made as holy as the temple's sacred bowls.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] will then be king over all the earth. In that day the LORD [Yahweh] will be seen as one with a single name.”
